transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop thinking about how old and wrong my face looks, and it’s getting in the way of me moving up at work. I've worked so hard at my job, but this worry is starting to hold me back from a promotion.

Do you spend a lot of time checking, hiding, or trying to fix parts of your face because you feel they look defective, or is the main problem that you feel embarrassed and judged by other people in social situations?

Yes, I spend 20 to 30 minutes every morning in the mirror pulling my skin back, trying different makeup, taking selfies, and constantly asking my husband for reassurance. I only avoid things like work presentations or my book club because of how old and wrong my face looks, rather than a general fear of being judged by others.

Do you ever feel completely certain that your face is actually deformed or looks wrong, even when other people tell you it looks normal? Or do you recognize that this might be exaggerated by your own worries?

When I look in the mirror, I feel completely certain that my face looks sagging, aged, and just wrong. Even though my husband and clients tell me I look normal, what I see feels like an undeniable reality to me in those moments. It is just so hard to believe them, which is why I keep asking for reassurance.

F42.2 seems less likely because the symptoms are not centered on varied obsessions/compulsions but on a fixed appearance-related preoccupation with poor or absent insight.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient shows a persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (face looking old, sagging, and wrong) that others do not observe, along with repetitive appearance-related behaviors including mirror checking, skin pulling, makeup attempts, taking selfies, and reassurance seeking. The concern causes avoidance of presentations and interferes with occupational advancement. Her conviction reaches delusional intensity at times, but this is captured within body dysmorphic disorder in ICD-10 somatoform/hypochondriacal disorder coding.
